transcribe_prompt: Okay Tesla, you make the Roadster. Megapacks, Plumpton. Raspberry Pi, Arduino, firmware, Linux. Boot ID, reset cause, buck converter. CAN bus. Deakin. Manit Khera.

lines.text: Okay, Tesla. You make the Roadster.
lines.action: deadpan, then eyes follow the Roadster: his left, up, his right, about 3 s (keep the whole look)

lines.text: I made a car too. It's slightly smaller.
lines.action: small grin, then hold still looking slightly down, 2 s (keep the hold)

lines.text: I'm Manit, third-year Software Engineering student at Deakin, built it to carry the laundry under cover when it rains, it runs firmware I wrote on an Arduino
sends its data to a Raspberry Pi running Linux every five seconds, but every so often it would just restart, at random
lines.action: straight face on 'at random', hold 1 s

lines.text: could have swapped parts until it stopped, instead went back through the data, boot ID and reset cause pointed to the power dropping out, led me to a failing buck converter
after that I stopped waiting for things to break, before I trusted it I tried to break it on purpose, fake faulty data and tests in the wet
your Megapacks are a much bigger version of that, 444 at Plumpton, this role tests a site before it goes live and builds tools that catch a fault before the customer sees any downtime
I haven't worked with CAN bus or battery systems yet, that's what I'd want to learn from your team
So yeah, I'm Manit Khera. No flips yet, but I'll always check the data. Thanks for watching.
